Test_Objective: An unauthenticated visitor must not reach the profile page, because /profile is a private route (absent from PUBLIC_ROUTES in proxy.ts) unlike the public /kudos board.
Precondition: No active session (signed out).
Steps:
1. Clear cookies.
2. Navigate to /profile.
Expected_Result: The user is redirected to /login. No profile content, name, department or Kudos counters are rendered at any point.
Note: The page also re-checks the session itself as defense in depth, so this holds even if the proxy route list is edited.

Test_Objective: A signed-in Sunner opening /profile with no query string sees their OWN profile.
Precondition: Signed in as a Sunner with a roster profile row.
Steps:
1. Sign in.
2. Navigate to /profile with no query string.
Expected_Result: The page renders the signed-in Sunner's own profile: their avatar, full name, department, Hero tier badge and hoa-thi stars in the keyvisual hero; the badge collection; the personal statistics card; and the KUDOS section.

Test_Objective: /profile?id={profileId} renders THAT Sunner's profile, which is the link the live board already emits when a name is clicked.
Precondition: Signed in. A second Sunner exists on the roster with at least one received Kudo.
Steps:
1. Sign in as Sunner A.
2. Navigate to /profile?id={Sunner B's profile id}.
Expected_Result: The hero shows Sunner B's avatar, name, department, Hero tier and hoa-thi stars. The page is Sunner B's profile, not Sunner A's.
Note: Source of the link: app/kudos/use-board-interactions.ts -> openProfile.

Test_Objective: An ?id that names the viewer themselves must canonicalize to the SELF view, so copying your own profile link does not show you a stranger's version of your own page.
Precondition: Signed in as Sunner A, who knows their own profile id.
Steps:
1. Sign in as Sunner A.
2. Navigate to /profile?id={Sunner A's own profile id}.
Expected_Result: The page renders the SELF view, identical to /profile with no query string: the statistics card is shown (not a write-Kudo bar), the badge heading is the first-person variant, and the KUDOS dropdown offers both directions.
Note: Recorded as an assumption in the plan's clarifications.md.

Test_Objective: An ?id that is a well-formed UUID but matches no profile returns 404, not a server error.
Precondition: Signed in.
Steps:
1. Sign in.
2. Navigate to /profile with a syntactically valid UUID that belongs to no profile.
Expected_Result: The 404 page is shown. No 500, no unhandled error, no partially rendered profile.

Test_Objective: A malformed ?id must be rejected before it reaches the database, since a non-UUID sent to a uuid column raises Postgres 22P02 and would otherwise surface as a 500.
Precondition: Signed in.
Steps:
1. Sign in.
2. Navigate to /profile with each malformed id in turn.
Expected_Result: Every case returns the 404 page. No 500 and no database error text is ever shown.
Note: The id is shape-checked against a canonical UUID pattern before any query is issued.

Test_Objective: An empty ?id means 'no id' (the self view), while a REPEATED ?id is refused rather than having one value silently picked.
Precondition: Signed in.
Steps:
1. Navigate to /profile?id= (empty value).
2. Navigate to /profile?id={idA}&id={idB} with two different ids.
Expected_Result: Step 1 renders the viewer's own profile (a cleared query string is not an error). Step 2 returns 404 — two different ids in one request is not a page that was asked for, and choosing one would hide the mistake.

Test_Objective: The hero renders the keyvisual banner with the viewer's avatar, name, department, Hero tier badge and hoa-thi stars, per mms_A / A.1 / A.2 / A.3 and mms_3_Keyvisual.
Precondition: Signed in as a Sunner with a department, at least 1 distinct sender and at least 10 received Kudos.
Steps:
1. Navigate to /profile.
2. Inspect the hero block.
Expected_Result: The keyvisual artwork banner is shown. Below it: the circular avatar, the full name in gold, then the department, the Hero tier badge and the hoa-thi stars on one row. The banner shows artwork only — no duplicated navigation bar and no second avatar or name ghosted behind the live ones.
Note: Hero tier is keyed on DISTINCT SENDERS; hoa-thi stars on TOTAL Kudos received (10/20/50). Two different denominators, deliberately.

Test_Objective: The badge collection shows all 6 slots (B2-B7) greyed out, using the real badge artwork desaturated rather than blank placeholders, because the Secret Box that awards them is deferred.
Precondition: Signed in.
Steps:
1. Navigate to /profile.
2. Inspect the badge row below the hero.
Expected_Result: Exactly 6 badge circles are rendered, in the design's fixed order, each showing its real badge image desaturated/greyed. No slot appears unlocked and no slot is hidden.
Note: Driven by an unlocked-badge list that is always empty today, so the slots light up later with no reshaping.

Test_Objective: The badge-row heading is first-person on your own profile and neutral on someone else's, since the possessive would be wrong above another person's badges.
Precondition: Signed in. A second Sunner exists.
Steps:
1. Navigate to /profile and read the badge heading.
2. Navigate to /profile?id={other} and read it again.
Expected_Result: Step 1 shows the first-person heading (VN 'Bo suu tap icon cua toi' / EN 'My icon collection'). Step 2 shows the neutral heading (VN 'Bo suu tap icon' / EN 'Icon collection').
Note: Both keys ship in locales/{vi,en}/profile.json; a parity test asserts they stay distinct.

Test_Objective: The statistics card (mms_B) renders the viewer's five counters with second-person labels, and appears ONLY on their own profile.
Precondition: Signed in as a Sunner with known counters.
Steps:
1. Navigate to /profile.
2. Read every row of the statistics card.
Expected_Result: Five rows are shown with the viewer's real numbers: Kudos received, Kudos sent, hearts received, then a divider, then Secret Boxes opened and Secret Boxes unopened. Each value matches the viewer's actual counters.
Note: Labels are second-person ('bạn'), which is why the whole card is replaced rather than reused on another profile.

Test_Objective: The two Secret Box rows read 0 and the 'Mo Secret Box' button is disabled, matching the live board's sidebar — the honest rendering of a deferred feature rather than invented numbers or hidden rows.
Precondition: Signed in.
Steps:
1. Navigate to /profile.
2. Inspect the two Secret Box rows and the button below them.
3. Attempt to click the button.
Expected_Result: 'Secret Boxes opened' and 'Secret Boxes unopened' both show 0. The 'Mo Secret Box' button is rendered but disabled, and clicking it does nothing — no dialog, no navigation, no error.
Note: Same deferral as the board sidebar's prize rows.

Test_Objective: On another Sunner's profile the WHOLE statistics card is replaced by a write-Kudo bar, in the same slot (item 107677 / mms_B_Thong ke), modelled on the board's write bar.
Precondition: Signed in as Sunner A. Sunner B exists.
Steps:
1. Navigate to /profile?id={Sunner B}.
2. Inspect the area where the statistics card sits on your own profile.
Expected_Result: A write-Kudo bar is shown in that position, naming Sunner B (VN 'Gui loi cam on va ghi nhan den {name}'). No statistics row, no counters and no 'Mo Secret Box' button appear anywhere on the page.
Note: Driven by one data-level branch (stats is null for anyone but the caller), so the self/other distinction is decided once.

Test_Objective: The write-Kudo bar opens the existing Viet Kudo modal with the viewed Sunner already selected as recipient, since the viewer has already indicated who they meant.
Precondition: Signed in as Sunner A. Sunner B exists.
Steps:
1. Navigate to /profile?id={Sunner B}.
2. Click the write-Kudo bar.
3. Inspect the recipient field.
Expected_Result: The Viet Kudo modal opens with Sunner B's name already in the recipient field. No recipient-suggestion list is popped open over the untouched field. The field remains editable, so the recipient can still be changed.
Note: Implemented as an optional prop defaulting to null, so the homepage and board compose flows are unchanged.

Test_Objective: Your own profile offers no write-Kudo bar, because a Sunner cannot send themselves a Kudo.
Precondition: Signed in.
Steps:
1. Navigate to /profile.
2. Look for a write-Kudo bar.
Expected_Result: No write-Kudo bar is rendered; the statistics card occupies that slot instead.
Note: The database also refuses a self-Kudo (kudos_no_self), but the surface should not invite the attempt.

Test_Objective: On your own profile the KUDOS dropdown offers both 'Da nhan (N)' and 'Da gui (N)', with counts from the profile counters, and Received is selected first.
Precondition: Signed in as a Sunner who has both received and sent Kudos.
Steps:
1. Navigate to /profile.
2. Read the dropdown trigger.
3. Open the dropdown.
Expected_Result: The trigger initially reads 'Da nhan (N)' with N equal to the viewer's received count. Opening it lists exactly two options: 'Da nhan (N)' and 'Da gui (M)', where M is the viewer's sent count.
Note: The trigger shows the ACTIVE direction, as the design writes it.

Sub_Sub_Category: Sent is hidden on another profile
Test_Objective: Another Sunner's profile must offer Received ONLY. Their sent count includes Kudos they sent ANONYMOUSLY, which no feed will ever show — so publishing that number, or a Sent list that contradicts it, would leak how many anonymous Kudos they sent.
Precondition: Signed in as Sunner A. Sunner B exists and has sent at least one ANONYMOUS Kudo.
Steps:
1. Navigate to /profile?id={Sunner B}.
2. Open the KUDOS direction dropdown.
3. Search the whole page for any 'Da gui' text.
Expected_Result: The dropdown contains exactly ONE option, 'Da nhan (N)'. No 'Da gui' option, label or count appears anywhere on the page. Sunner B's sent count is never rendered.
Note: The leak is closed by removing the surface, not by adjusting the count. This is the single most important case on this screen.

Test_Objective: Your own Sent list must include the Kudos you sent anonymously, and show YOU as their author — the public feed masks the sender, so a naive sent-by filter would silently drop them and under-report against the counter beside it.
Precondition: Signed in as Sunner A, who has sent at least one signed and one ANONYMOUS Kudo.
Steps:
1. Navigate to /profile.
2. Switch the KUDOS dropdown to 'Da gui'.
3. Compare the number of cards to the count in the dropdown label.
Expected_Result: Both the signed and the anonymous Kudo appear. The card count matches the 'Da gui (N)' count. On your own sent cards you are shown as the author — the masked-alias placeholder is NOT used for your own anonymous Kudo, though it is still marked as having been sent anonymously.
Note: Served by a caller-scoped definer view whose WHERE clause is the security boundary.

Test_Objective: Two different signed-in Sunners asking for a Sent list must each see only their own Kudos, with no way to request another person's.
Precondition: Two Sunners, A and B, each having sent at least one Kudo (A's including an anonymous one).
Steps:
1. Sign in as Sunner A, open /profile and switch to 'Da gui'. Record the cards.
2. Sign in as Sunner B in a separate session and repeat.
3. Compare the two lists.
Expected_Result: The two lists are disjoint. Sunner B never sees any of Sunner A's sent Kudos, including A's anonymous one, and vice versa. There is no request that returns another Sunner's sent list.
Note: Must be checked with two live sessions; a single-session test cannot demonstrate it.

Test_Objective: Cards in the profile feed are identical in shape and behaviour to the same Kudo on the live board, including the masking of anonymous senders on a Received list.
Precondition: Signed in. The viewed Sunner has received at least one signed and one anonymous Kudo.
Steps:
1. Navigate to a profile with received Kudos.
2. Compare a card against the same Kudo on /kudos.
Expected_Result: Sender, recipient, title, body, timestamp, hashtags, attachments, heart count and Copy Link all render as they do on the board. An anonymous Kudo shows the masked alias instead of the sender's name — the sender's identity, department and counters are all withheld.
Note: Same mapper and same column list as the board, so the two cannot diverge.

Test_Objective: Switching direction loads page 1 of the newly chosen list and discards the pages accumulated by infinite scroll for the previous one.
Precondition: Signed in as a Sunner with more than one page of received Kudos and at least one sent Kudo.
Steps:
1. Navigate to /profile.
2. Scroll until at least a second page of Received has loaded.
3. Switch the dropdown to 'Da gui'.
Expected_Result: The feed is replaced by page 1 of the Sent list. No Received cards remain stacked below it. The trigger label updates to 'Da gui (N)' only once the new page has actually loaded, never before.

Test_Objective: Re-selecting the direction that is already active is a no-op, not a clear — there is no unfiltered state for this list to fall back to.
Precondition: Signed in, viewing /profile with Received active and at least one card.
Steps:
1. Open the KUDOS dropdown.
2. Click the already-selected 'Da nhan (N)' option.
Expected_Result: The dropdown closes and the feed is unchanged — the same cards remain and no request is issued. The list does not blank.

Test_Objective: Each direction shows its OWN empty message, because 'no Kudos yet' and 'you have not sent any' are different facts.
Precondition: A Sunner with no received Kudos, and a Sunner with no sent Kudos.
Steps:
1. Open the profile of a Sunner with no received Kudos.
2. On your own profile with nothing sent, switch to 'Da gui'.
Expected_Result: Step 1 shows the received empty copy (VN 'Hien tai chua co Kudos nao.'). Step 2 shows the distinct sent empty copy (VN 'Ban chua gui Kudos nao.'). Neither shows a bare, empty feed area.
Note: The received wording matches the board's verbatim.

Test_Objective: The profile feed pages by infinite scroll, reusing the board's keyset cursor so no card is duplicated or skipped while new Kudos arrive.
Precondition: Signed in. The viewed Sunner has more than 10 received Kudos.
Steps:
1. Navigate to that profile.
2. Scroll to the bottom of the feed repeatedly.
Expected_Result: Further pages load automatically as the bottom is approached, 10 cards at a time. No card appears twice and none is skipped. When the last page is reached, an end-of-feed message is shown instead of a loading indicator.

Test_Objective: Hearting from the profile page behaves exactly as on the board, including the refusal on your own Kudo, because it goes through the same server action.
Precondition: Signed in. A card by another Sunner and a card sent by the viewer are both reachable.
Steps:
1. Heart a Kudo sent by someone else.
2. Heart it again to withdraw.
3. Attempt to heart a Kudo you sent yourself (visible in your Sent list).
Expected_Result: Steps 1 and 2 toggle the heart and the count updates to the value the SERVER reports, not a locally incremented one. Step 3 is refused with the same message the board shows for hearting your own Kudo.
Note: Reuses the board's existing action untouched; the server enforces both refusals regardless of the UI.

Test_Objective: A hashtag click leads to the board filtered by that tag, and Copy Link copies a shareable link to the Kudo.
Precondition: Signed in, viewing a profile with at least one hashtagged Kudo.
Steps:
1. Click a hashtag on a profile card.
2. Return and click Copy Link on a card.
Expected_Result: Step 1 navigates to the live board filtered by that hashtag (the profile has no hashtag filter of its own). Step 2 copies the Kudo's link and confirms with the board's copy toast.
Note: The board already answers 'who else was thanked for this', which is what clicking a tag is asking.

Test_Objective: The orange 'Spam' chip (mms_D.3.1_Status) is never rendered, because no moderation model exists in the schema or the specs.
Precondition: Signed in, viewing any profile with Kudos.
Steps:
1. Navigate to a profile with several Kudos.
2. Inspect every card for a status chip.
Expected_Result: No 'Spam' chip appears on any card, in either direction, in any state.
Note: A typed status field is carried on the card shape so the chip can be enabled later without reshaping anything.

Test_Objective: Every string on the page is translated in both languages, with the counts and the recipient name substituted correctly.
Precondition: Signed in.
Steps:
1. Open /profile in Vietnamese and read every label.
2. Switch to English and repeat.
3. Repeat both on another Sunner's profile.
Expected_Result: No blank labels and no untranslated keys in either language. Direction labels show their counts (e.g. 'Received (12)'), and the write bar names the viewed Sunner. Statistics labels match the wording used by the live board's sidebar.
Note: Key-set parity between the two bundles is asserted by an automated test.

Test_Objective: A roster profile whose owner has never signed in — no avatar, no department, no Kudos — still renders without broken elements.
Precondition: A roster profile with null avatar, null department and zero Kudos.
Steps: 1. Navigate to that profile.
Expected_Result: The page renders: a placeholder avatar circle, the name, no department line, no Hero tier badge and no hoa-thi stars (zero Kudos means no badge, which differs from the lowest badge). The badge row still shows 6 greyed slots and the feed shows the received empty copy.

Test_Objective: The profile page is read-only apart from the pre-existing heart action, and never exposes email or auth identifiers.
Precondition: Signed in.
Steps:
1. Open /profile and /profile?id={other}.
2. Look for any edit affordance on the name, avatar or department.
3. Inspect the page payload for email addresses or auth user ids.
Expected_Result: No edit control is offered anywhere, on either face of the route. No email address and no auth user id appears in the rendered page or its data payload.
Note: Editing was explicitly ruled out even though the schema permits it; only the allowed profile columns are ever selected.
